summary: 1 was the owner of the suit properties. The predecessor in interest of the respondents, who was a tenant of the suit properties, filed a suit for eviction of the tenant on the ground of default in payment of rent. The trial court decreed the suit. The first appellate court, however, allowed the appeal and decreed the suit. The first appellate court, however, held that the tenant was not entitled to the benefit of section 14(1)(e) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, as the tenant had not paid the rent in spite of notice served on him and, therefore, the suit was not maintainable. The High Court, however, held that the tenant was not entitled to the benefit of section 14(1)(e) of the Act. In the appeal to this Court, it was contended on behalf of the tenant that the High Court was wrong in holding that the tenant was not entitled to the benefit of section 14(1)(e) of the Act because, the tenant had not paid the rent in spite of notice served on him and, therefore, the suit was not maintainable. Dismissing the appeal, ^ HELD: 1. The High Court was right in holding that the tenant was not entitled to the benefit of section 14(1)(e) of the Act. [765C] 2. The High Court was right in holding that the tenant was not entitled to the benefit of section 14(1)(e) of the Act. [765D] 3.
